practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to nominate members to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons of the Rajya Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha nominates members from amongst the members of the House to a panel of Vice-Chairpersons.

practiceQuestions.q: When does a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons preside over the Rajya Sabha?
opts: When the Prime Minister is absent
When both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman are absent
During the introduction of a Money Bill
practiceQuestions.sol: A member of the panel of Vice-Chairpersons can preside over the House only when both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman are absent from a sitting of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum number of members typically nominated to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons of the Rajya Sabha under the rules?
opts: No fixed limit exists in the Constitution
practiceQuestions.sol: Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha provides that the Chairman nominates from amongst the members of the House a panel of not more than ten vices-chairpersons.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional provision provides for the office of the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, distinct from the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 89 of the Constitution of India provides for the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Panel of Vice-Chairpersons, however, is a procedural creation under the Rules of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons preside over the House when a resolution for the removal of the Chairman is under consideration?
opts: Only with the permission of the Prime Minister
Yes, if the Deputy Chairman also resigns
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 92 of the Constitution, the Chairman (or Deputy Chairman) shall not preside while a resolution for their removal is under consideration. While Article 92 mentions the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, rule-based panel members also cannot preside over such a sitting.

practiceQuestions.q: Does a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons receive a special salary or allowance solely by virtue of being on the panel?
opts: Yes, equivalent to a Cabinet Minister
Yes, equivalent to the Deputy Chairman
No, they only receive normal allowances as Members of Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: Members of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons do not receive any additional salary or allowances merely for being on the panel; they draw their regular salaries and allowances as MPs.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons when the Rajya Sabha is dissolved?
opts: It is automatically reconstituted by the new President
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not dissolved
All members must be re-elected through general elections
The panel takes over executive functions temporarily
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution under Article 83(1). Therefore, the question of dissolution does not apply to it or its panels in the manner of the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: When presiding over the Rajya Sabha, does a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons have the same powers as the Chairman?
opts: Yes, while presiding, they have all the powers of the Chairman
They can only adjourn the House, nothing else

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following documents contains the rule establishing the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons?
opts: Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha
The Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act
practiceQuestions.sol: The Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is created under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), formulated under Article 118 of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: If both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman are absent, and no member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is present, who presides over the Rajya Sabha?
opts: The senior-most Cabinet Minister in the House
The House determines another member to preside
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the rules, if the Chairman, Deputy Chairman, and all members of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons are absent, the House may appoint any other member to preside.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons necessary even though there is a constitutionally recognized Deputy Chairman in the Rajya Sabha?
opts: Because the Deputy Chairman cannot vote in the House under any circumstance
To ensure uninterrupted functioning of the House when both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman are unavailable due to illness, foreign visits, or simultaneous engagements
Because the Deputy Chairman's office is filled by presidential nomination only
To check the arbitrary powers of the Chairman
practiceQuestions.sol: Legislative business requires continuous presiding officers. Since both the Chairman (who is the Vice-President of India with heavy executive and ceremonial duties) and the Deputy Chairman can be absent simultaneously, a panel of Vice-Chairpersons ensures seamless continuity.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the tenure of a member on the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons differ structurally from that of the Deputy Chairman?
opts: Panel members have a fixed 6-year tenure, while the Deputy Chairman serves for 5 years
The Deputy Chairman has a fixed constitutional term of 6 years (unless they cease to be a member), whereas panel members serve at the pleasure of the Chairman and can be reconstituted anytime
Panel members are elected by proportional representation
There is no difference in their tenure provisions
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Rajya Sabha for a term of up to 6 years. Conversely, members of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons are nominated by the Chairman and hold their positions as panel members as per the Chairman's discretion and rule provisions.

practiceQuestions.q: In terms of constitutional status, how does the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons compare with the Panel of Chairpersons in the Lok Sabha?
opts: Lok Sabha panel is constitutional, Rajya Sabha panel is statutory
Both are analogous procedural mechanisms established under the respective Rules of Procedure of both Houses
Lok Sabha panel has voting powers, while Rajya Sabha panel does not
Rajya Sabha panel members are appointed by the President, Lok Sabha panel by the Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: Both panels serve the exact same functional purpose in their respective houses—to preside in the absence of principal presiding officers—and both are creatures of the internal rules of procedure (Rule 8 in Rajya Sabha, Rule 9 in Lok Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the implication when a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is presiding over the House during a voting process?
opts: They can exercise a casting vote on any matter
They cannot vote in the first instance, but exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie
They retain their regular vote as an MP and cannot cast a casting vote
They must resign from the panel before voting
practiceQuestions.sol: Like the Chairman or Deputy Chairman, a person presiding (including a panel member) does not vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote in the event of a tie to break the deadlock.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha be appointed to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons?
opts: No, only directly elected members are eligible
Yes, nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are fully eligible to be on the panel and preside over the House
Only if they join a political party first
No, because they cannot vote in the election of the Deputy Chairman
practiceQuestions.sol: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are members of the House and have been appointed to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons historically, exercising all presiding functions when called upon.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the inclusion of women or diverse regional representation in the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons impact parliamentary governance?
opts: It promotes inclusive leadership, broadens institutional legitimacy, and sets precedents for gender and regional parity in higher parliamentary offices
It reduces the term of the Rajya Sabha
It violates the principle of seniority
practiceQuestions.sol: Recent practice of including women parliamentarians (and diverse members) in the panel reflects inclusive governance, signaling broader representation in running legislative affairs.

practiceQuestions.q: If a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons resigns from their political party, does it automatically terminate their position on the panel?
opts: Yes, party membership is mandatory for panel members
No, the panel position is held at the discretion of the Chairman, independent of party affiliation changes, unless disqualified under anti-defection law
Yes, the President terminates the panel membership
The Supreme Court decides their continuation
practiceQuestions.sol: Panel membership is an internal administrative nomination by the Chairman. Political party changes do not automatically revoke panel status unless the member suffers disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) or resigns.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary distinction between the powers of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha and a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons while presiding?
opts: Panel members cannot sign bills passed by the House
There is no functional distinction in powers while occupying the chair; both exercise identical authority during that sitting
Panel members cannot adjourn the House
Chairman has executive powers, panel members only have judicial powers
practiceQuestions.sol: While occupying the chair, a member of the panel of Vice-Chairpersons has the same powers and responsibilities as the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons determine whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
opts: Yes, with the Chairman's written consent
No, the certification of a Money Bill is exclusively vested in the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 110(3)
Yes, while presiding over a joint sitting
Only if authorized by the Finance Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: Money Bills originate only in the Lok Sabha, and Article 110(3) explicitly vests the power to certify a Money Bill solely in the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha (and its presiding officers) does not certify Money Bills.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Rajya Sabha require a multi-member panel of Vice-Chairpersons rather than just a single Deputy Chairman?
opts: To comply with international parliamentary standards
To ensure that if the Chairman and Deputy Chairman are simultaneously unavailable or busy with other constitutional duties, parliamentary proceedings do not halt
To provide ministerial berths to senior members
To conduct elections for the Vice-President
practiceQuestions.sol: A single Deputy Chairman may also fall ill, be absent, or have personal/official engagements. A multi-member panel ensures availability of presiding officers at all times during legislative sessions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The panel is constituted under the provisions of the Constitution of India.
2. The members of the panel are nominated by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is created under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha, not directly by a constitutional article. Statement 2 is correct: the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha nominates panel members.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons cannot preside over the House when the office of the Chairman is vacant.
2. When presiding over the Rajya Sabha, a member of the panel has the same powers as the Chairman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 91(1), when the office of Chairman is vacant, the duties of the office are performed by the Deputy Chairman, or if that is also vacant, by a member appointed by the President. Panel members preside in the *absence* of the Chairman/Deputy Chairman, not when the Chairman's office itself is vacant (vacancies are governed by Article 91). Statement 2 is correct; while presiding, panel members have identical powers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding presiding officers of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The maximum number of members on the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is fixed by the Constitution at ten.
2. Members of the panel receive a special monthly salary drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the limit of ten members is fixed by the Rules of Procedure of Rajya Sabha, not the Constitution. Statement 2 is wrong because panel members do not receive any special salary distinct from their regular MP salaries.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the House.
2. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons can preside over the House even when the Deputy Chairman is present.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the Chairman of Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President of India) is NOT a member of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is wrong because panel members can only preside when BOTH the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman are absent.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of a presiding officer in the Rajya Sabha:
1. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons can exercise the power to accept a motion for adjournment of the House.
2. Panel members are immune from judicial review for any procedural ruling given while presiding over the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 is correct because while presiding, a panel member exercises all powers of the Chairman, including accepting motions. Statement 2 is correct under Article 122, which protects parliamentary proceedings and presiding officers' procedural rulings from being questioned in any court.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The office of the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha is mentioned in the Constitution.
2. The Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is mentioned in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 89 provides for the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is not mentioned in the Constitution text; it is created under the internal Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal or vacation of office:
1. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons ceases to be on the panel if they cease to be a member of the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha must consult the Prime Minister before nominating members to the panel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct because panel members must be members of the House; if their term ends or they resign from Rajya Sabha, they leave the panel. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Chairman's power to nominate panel members is an independent prerogative under the House rules and does not require mandatory consultation with the Prime Minister.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can nominate opposition party members as well as ruling party members to the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons.
2. The Panel of Vice-Chairpersons includes representatives from diverse political backgrounds to foster bipartisan consensus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Historically and procedurally, the panel is drawn from various parties (ruling and opposition) to ensure smooth, non-partisan conduct of House proceedings, embodying a collaborative parliamentary approach.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the voting rights of presiding officers in Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha can vote in the first instance.
2. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons, when presiding, cannot vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in the event of a tie.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) is not a member of the House and therefore never has a vote (except casting vote if applicable, but as Vice-President he doesn't vote as MP). Statement 2 is correct: any presiding officer (including panel members) refrains from first-instance voting and uses only a casting vote.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning parliamentary committees and presiding panels:
1. A member of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons cannot be appointed as the Chairperson of any Parliamentary Committee.
2. The rules governing the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons in Rajya Sabha are framed under Article 118 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because panel members are senior MPs who frequently serve as chairpersons or members of various Parliamentary Committees (like Standing Committees). Statement 2 is correct: Article 118 empowers each House of Parliament to make rules for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business, under which the Rajya Sabha rules establishing the panel are framed.
